chunks.heading: When You Know to Much
chunks.notes: The repeated "It pains me to know..." openers are anaphora, the piece pivots through stacked rhetorical questions about myth/childhood, and the content is explicitly about squandered creative potential and time/aging.

chunks.heading: When You Know to Much
chunks.notes: "You called it destiny. You called it talent..." and the "Let me laugh... Let me spit..." run are anaphoric, the speaker reckons with being mocked/"defiled" and reclaims worth through defiant self-assertion, closing on the aphoristic "My words aren't great. They're mine."
